files.bootstrap/appsets/cluster-apps.yaml:
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: ApplicationSet
metadata:
  name: cluster-apps
  namespace: argocd
  annotations:
    # See config-apps.yaml: argocd-diff-preview filters ApplicationSets by their OWN
    # metadata.annotations *before* expanding them, so this coarse gate is required
    # in addition to the per-Application pattern in spec.template below.
    # Keep it as the union of the patterns spec.template can render.
    argocd-diff-preview/watch-pattern: '^infrastructure/.*, ^services/.*, ^templates/.*'
spec:
  goTemplate: true
  goTemplateOptions: ["missingkey=error"]
  generators:
    - matrix:
        generators:
          - list:
              elements:
                # deployPhaseDefault is the fallback when an app.yaml doesn't set deployPhase explicitly.
                # Apps SHOULD set it explicitly for clarity (see infrastructure/*/app.yaml).
                - category: infrastructure
                  pathPattern: "infrastructure/**/app.yaml"
                  deployPhaseDefault: controllers
                  commonValues: ""
                  defaultChartRepo: ""
                  defaultChartName: ""
                  defaultChartVersion: ""
                - category: services
                  pathPattern: "services/**/app.yaml"
                  deployPhaseDefault: services
                  commonValues: "templates/common.yaml"
                  defaultChartRepo: "https://bjw-s-labs.github.io/helm-charts"
                  defaultChartName: "app-template"
                  defaultChartVersion: "5.2.1"
          - git:
              repoURL: https://github.com/Starktastic-Homelab/apps.git
              revision: HEAD
              files:
                - path: "{{ .pathPattern }}"
  strategy:
    type: RollingSync
    rollingSync:
      steps:
        - matchExpressions:
            - key: deploy-phase
              operator: In
              values:
                - crds
        - matchExpressions:
            - key: deploy-phase
              operator: In
              values:
                - foundation
        - matchExpressions:
            - key: deploy-phase
              operator: In
              values:
                - controllers
        - matchExpressions:
            - key: deploy-phase
              operator: In
              values:
                - services
  template:
    metadata:
      name: "{{.name}}"
      namespace: argocd
      finalizers: ["resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io"]
      labels:
        deploy-phase: '{{ dig "deployPhase" .deployPhaseDefault . }}'
      annotations:
        notifications.argoproj.io/subscribe.on-sync-failed.ntfy: ""
        notifications.argoproj.io/subscribe.on-health-degraded.ntfy: ""
        # Anchored: unanchored 'templates/.*' also matches every app's own
        # manifests/templates/ dir, which selected all 74 apps on any such PR.
        argocd-diff-preview/watch-pattern: '^{{.path.path}}/.*, ^templates/.*'
    spec:
      project: default
      sources: []
      destination:
        server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
        namespace: "{{ .namespace }}"
      syncPolicy:
        automated:
          prune: true
          selfHeal: true
        syncOptions:
          - CreateNamespace=true
          - ServerSideApply=true
          - RespectIgnoreDifferences=true
        retry:
          limit: 30
          backoff:
            duration: 15s
            factor: 2
            maxDuration: 5m
      ignoreDifferences:
        - group: ""
          kind: Secret
          jsonPointers:
            - /data
        - group: apps
          kind: Deployment
          jqPathExpressions:
            - '.spec.template.metadata.annotations["checksum/lapi-secret"]'
            - '.spec.template.metadata.annotations["checksum/lapi-configmap"]'
            # Stakater Reloader stamps this on restart; without ignoring it,
            # selfHeal strips it and Reloader re-adds it, forever.
            - '.spec.template.metadata.annotations["reloader.stakater.com/last-reloaded-from"]'
        # Reloader runs with autoReloadAll, so it stamps StatefulSets and
        # DaemonSets too — Traefik is a DaemonSet, and the monitoring and
        # logging charts generate both kinds.
        - group: apps
          kind: StatefulSet
          jqPathExpressions:
            - '.spec.template.metadata.annotations["reloader.stakater.com/last-reloaded-from"]'
        - group: apps
          kind: DaemonSet
          jqPathExpressions:
            - '.spec.template.metadata.annotations["reloader.stakater.com/last-reloaded-from"]'
  templatePatch: |
    {{- $repo := "https://github.com/Starktastic-Homelab/apps.git" }}
    {{- $isService := eq .category "services" }}
    {{- $basePath := dig "baseApp" "" . }}
    {{- $valuesPath := or $basePath (printf "%s" .path.path) }}
    {{- $hasCommon := ne .commonValues "" }}
    {{- $extras := dig "commonValuesExtras" (list) . }}
    spec:
      sources:
        {{- if $isService }}
        - repoURL: '{{ dig "chart" "repo" .defaultChartRepo . }}'
          chart: '{{ dig "chart" "name" .defaultChartName . }}'
          targetRevision: '{{ dig "chart" "version" .defaultChartVersion . }}'
          helm:
            valueFiles:
              - $values/templates/globals.yaml
              {{- if $hasCommon }}
              - $values/{{ .commonValues }}
              {{- end }}
              {{- range $extras }}
              - $values/{{ . }}
              {{- end }}
              - $values/{{ $valuesPath }}/values.yaml
              {{- if and $basePath (dig "valuesOverride" false .) }}
              - $values/{{.path.path}}/values.yaml
              {{- end }}
        {{- else }}
        - repoURL: "{{ .chart.repo }}"
          chart: "{{ .chart.name }}"
          targetRevision: "{{ .chart.version }}"
          helm:
            valueFiles:
              - $values/templates/globals.yaml
              {{- if $hasCommon }}
              - $values/{{ .commonValues }}
              {{- end }}
              {{- range $extras }}
              - $values/{{ . }}
              {{- end }}
              - $values/{{.path.path}}/values.yaml
        {{- end }}
        - repoURL: {{ $repo }}
          targetRevision: HEAD
          ref: values
        {{- if and $isService (dig "ingress" "enabled" false .) }}
        - repoURL: {{ $repo }}
          targetRevision: HEAD
          path: templates/ingress-chart
          helm:
            valueFiles:
              - $values/templates/globals.yaml
              {{- if $basePath }}
              - $values/{{ $basePath }}/app.yaml
              {{- end }}
              - $values/{{.path.path}}/app.yaml
        {{- end }}
        {{- if dig "manifests" false . }}
        {{- if dig "helmManifests" false . }}
        - repoURL: {{ $repo }}
          targetRevision: HEAD
          path: '{{.path.path}}/manifests'
          helm:
            valueFiles:
              - $values/templates/globals.yaml
        {{- else }}
        - repoURL: {{ $repo }}
          targetRevision: HEAD
          path: '{{.path.path}}/manifests'
        {{- end }}
        {{- end }}
files.bootstrap/appsets/config-apps.yaml:
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: ApplicationSet
metadata:
  name: config-apps
  namespace: argocd
  annotations:
    # argocd-diff-preview filters ApplicationSets by their OWN metadata.annotations
    # *before* expanding them into Applications, so this coarse gate is required in
    # addition to the per-Application pattern in spec.template below. Without it the
    # appset is skipped and every PR reports an empty diff.
    # Keep it as the union of the patterns spec.template can render.
    argocd-diff-preview/watch-pattern: '^infrastructure/base-configs/.*, ^infrastructure/configs/.*, ^templates/globals\.yaml'
spec:
  goTemplate: true
  goTemplateOptions: ["missingkey=error"]
  generators:
    - list:
        elements:
          - name: base-configs
            path: infrastructure/base-configs
          - name: infra-configs
            path: infrastructure/configs
  # No strategy: RollingSync would force autosync off on both Applications (see
  # the ArgoCDAppOutOfSync alert), and it bought no ordering here. base-configs is
  # storage PVs/PVCs plus backup CronJobs, infra-configs is IngressRoutes,
  # Middlewares and Certificates -- neither depends on the other. Ordering against
  # the CRD providers in cluster-apps was never provided anyway, since RollingSync
  # only sequences within a single ApplicationSet; spec.template's retry (30
  # attempts, backing off to 5m) is what actually covers that race.
  template:
    metadata:
      name: "{{.name}}"
      namespace: argocd
      finalizers: ["resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io"]
      annotations:
        notifications.argoproj.io/subscribe.on-sync-failed.ntfy: ""
        notifications.argoproj.io/subscribe.on-health-degraded.ntfy: ""
        argocd-diff-preview/watch-pattern: '^{{.path}}/.*, ^templates/globals\.yaml'
    spec:
      project: default
      sources:
        - repoURL: https://github.com/Starktastic-Homelab/apps.git
          targetRevision: HEAD
          path: "{{.path}}"
          helm:
            valueFiles:
              - $values/templates/globals.yaml
        - repoURL: https://github.com/Starktastic-Homelab/apps.git
          targetRevision: HEAD
          ref: values
      destination:
        server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
        namespace: default
      syncPolicy:
        automated:
          prune: true
          selfHeal: true
        syncOptions:
          - CreateNamespace=true
          - ServerSideApply=true
          - RespectIgnoreDifferences=true
        retry:
          limit: 30
          backoff:
            duration: 15s
            factor: 2
            maxDuration: 5m

apiVersion: v2
name: base-configs
description: Foundation configuration resources (storage PVs/PVCs, backup jobs)
type: application
version: 0.0.0
files.infrastructure/base-configs/templates/pg:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: pg-backup
  namespace: databases
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 3
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
            - name: pg-backup
              image: postgres:18.6-alpine@sha256:6c538e7206ea40ff740ef27883529390a690b6ead6ba96b44c67a9f7c638e8fd
              command: ["/bin/sh", "/scripts/backup.sh"]
              env:
                - name: PGHOST
                  value: postgres-postgresql.databases
                - name: PGPORT
                  value: "5432"
                - name: PGUSER
                  value: postgres
                - name: PGPASSWORD
                  valueFrom:
                    secretKeyRef:
                      name: postgres-admin-secret
                      key: postgres-password
              volumeMounts:
                - name: backup-storage
                  mountPath: /backup
                - name: script
                  mountPath: /scripts
                  readOnly: true
          volumes:
            - name: backup-storage
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: pg-backup
            - name: script
              configMap:
                name: pg-backup-script
                defaultMode: 0755

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: postgres-retained-startup-guard
  namespace: databases
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-1"
data:
  guard.sh: |
    #!/bin/bash
    # Identity guard only. RWOP attachment and verified VM retirement fence writers.
    set -eu
    export LC_ALL=C
    fail() {
      echo 'Retained PostgreSQL startup refused: data identity validation failed.' >&2
      exit 1
    }
    data=/bitnami/postgresql/data
    bin=/opt/bitnami/postgresql/bin/pg_controldata
    expected=${EXPECTED_SYSTEM_IDENTIFIER:-}
    # Canonical decimal identifiers only; the native identifier comparison also
    # rejects values outside uint64 range. Never infer the expectation from PGDATA.
    [[ $expected =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,19}$ ]] || fail
    [[ $("$bin" --version) == 'pg_controldata (PostgreSQL) 18.'* ]] || fail
    for directory in /bitnami/postgresql "$data" "$data/base" "$data/global" "$data/pg_wal"; do
      [ -d "$directory" ] && [ ! -L "$directory" ] && [ -r "$directory" ] && [ -x "$directory" ] || fail
    done
    for file in "$data/PG_VERSION" "$data/global/pg_control"; do
      [ -f "$file" ] && [ ! -L "$file" ] && [ -r "$file" ] || fail
    done
    [ "$(cat "$data/PG_VERSION")" = 18 ] || fail
    # PG18 stores an8192-byte control file; the native tool reads only its header.
    [ "$(stat -c %s "$data/global/pg_control")" = 8192 ] || fail
    # Test existence including dangling symlinks, before Bitnami can delete signals.
    for signal in standby.signal recovery.signal; do
      [ ! -e "$data/$signal" ] && [ ! -L "$data/$signal" ] || fail
    done
    scratch=$(mktemp -d)
    trap 'rm -rf "$scratch"' EXIT
    # Native pg_controldata may return0 despite a CRC warning. Reject all stderr.
    if ! timeout 30 "$bin" "$data" >"$scratch/control" 2>"$scratch/error"; then fail; fi
    [ ! -s "$scratch/error" ] || fail
    actual=$(awk '/^Database system identifier:[[:space:]]+[0-9]+$/ {print $NF}' "$scratch/control")
    [ "$actual" = "$expected" ] || fail
    # Leave a remaining postmaster.pid untouched; stock entrypoint handles restart
    # cleanup under the separately verified fencing contract. Do not initialize,
    # repair, chown or connect to this database here.
    echo 'Retained PostgreSQL data identity verified.'

# Inactive: install only during the separately approved stopped-writer operation.
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: postgres-storage-hold
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-6"
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false,Delete=false
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: [v1]
        operations: [CREATE, UPDATE]
        resources: [pods]
  matchConditions:
    - name: held-data-claim
      expression: >-
        object.metadata.namespace == 'databases' && has(object.spec.volumes) && object.spec.volumes.exists(v,
        has(v.persistentVolumeClaim) && v.persistentVolumeClaim.claimName == 'data-postgres-postgresql-0')
  validations:
    - expression: "false"
      message:
        The preserved PostgreSQL NFS claim is held. Restore acceptance is required before reopening any source writer.
---
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
metadata:
  name: postgres-storage-hold
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-6"
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false,Delete=false
spec:
  policyName: postgres-storage-hold
  validationActions: [Deny]

auth:
  existingSecret: postgres-admin-secret
  secretKeys:
    adminPasswordKey: postgres-password
# Since Bitnami's Aug-2025 registry change, bitnami/postgresql publishes only
# a rolling `:latest` - every other tag is a sha256 signature artifact, so
# there is no version to pin. Left alone, `latest` silently moves across
# PostgreSQL majors, and PostgreSQL refuses to start on a data directory
# written by a different major: the pod survives only while the old image
# stays cached on its node (pullPolicy IfNotPresent) and dies the moment it
# reschedules. It has already drifted once, moving glibc 2.36 -> 2.43 and
# invalidating every collation-dependent index.
# Pinning the digest is the only way to make this reproducible. Bump it
# deliberately, and run REINDEX + ALTER DATABASE ... REFRESH COLLATION
# VERSION afterwards if the base OS glibc changed.
# The digest lives in `tag` rather than the chart's own `image.digest` key so
# that Renovate can actually see it: its helm-values manager builds a
# dependency from repository+tag only, so a bare `digest:` is extracted as
# nothing and would sit here unwatched forever. In this form Renovate reads
# currentDigest and opens a digest-update PR, which renovate.json holds back
# from automerge so a human sizes up the major/glibc risk first.
# Docker resolves repo:tag@digest by digest, so the tag is cosmetic - do not
# also set image.digest, which would drop the tag and re-hide the dependency.
# The same treatment is applied to the other three images in this pod
# (os-shell, busybox, postgres-exporter) further down: all four are rolling
# tags, and any one of them breaking takes the whole database offline.
image:
  repository: bitnami/postgresql
  tag: "latest@sha256:b74b23f091dcc87041bcae557d840c36458af46b955279cb13aedec4c32d7f71"
primary:
  replicaCount: 1
  resourcesPreset: "none"
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 100m
      # Steady-state working set is ~265Mi; request must reflect that or the
      # scheduler overcommits the node.
      memory: 512Mi
    limits:
      cpu: "1"
      # Page cache counts against the cgroup limit, so usage sat pinned at
      # ~490Mi/512Mi (96%) for days and OOMKilled on any allocation spike,
      # taking every dependent app down with it. Retune if usage_bytes
      # (not working_set) again approaches the limit.
      memory: 1Gi
  persistence:
    existingClaim: postgres-data-block
    enabled: true
    # storageClass provided by global.storageClass in globals.yaml
    size: 8Gi
  livenessProbe:
    initialDelaySeconds: 60
    periodSeconds: 15
    timeoutSeconds: 10
    failureThreshold: 10
  readinessProbe:
    initialDelaySeconds: 10
    periodSeconds: 10
    timeoutSeconds: 10
    failureThreshold: 10
  startupProbe:
    enabled: true
    initialDelaySeconds: 30
    periodSeconds: 10
    timeoutSeconds: 10
    failureThreshold: 30
  initContainers:
    - name: verify-retained-data
      image: registry-1.docker.io/bitnami/postgresql:latest@sha256:b74b23f091dcc87041bcae557d840c36458af46b955279cb13aedec4c32d7f71
      imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      command:
        - /bin/bash
        - /retained-startup/guard.sh
      env:
        - name: EXPECTED_SYSTEM_IDENTIFIER
          value: "7584099661242523698"
      securityContext:
        runAsUser: 1001
        runAsGroup: 1001
        runAsNonRoot: true
        allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
        capabilities:
          drop:
            - ALL
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: 10m
          memory: 32Mi
        limits:
          cpu: 100m
          memory: 64Mi
      volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /bitnami/postgresql
          readOnly: true
        - name: retained-startup-guard
          mountPath: /retained-startup
          readOnly: true
        - name: retained-startup-scratch
          mountPath: /tmp
  extendedConfiguration: |
    # Peak observed usage is ~35 connections. 200 was never reachable within
    # the memory limit: worst case is max_connections x work_mem (4MB) of
    # sort/hash memory on top of shared_buffers, i.e. 800MB against a 1Gi cap.
    # 100 keeps >2x headroom over real usage while halving that exposure.
    max_connections = 100
    # Planner hint only, allocates nothing, but it was inherited as 4GB - 8x
    # the container's entire limit - so the planner assumed everything was
    # cached and under-costed index scans. Keep this ~50% of the memory limit.
    effective_cache_size = 512MB
  podSecurityContext:
    fsGroup: null
    enabled: true
  containerSecurityContext:
    runAsUser: 1001
    enabled: true
  extraVolumes:
    - name: retained-startup-guard
      configMap:
        name: postgres-retained-startup-guard
        defaultMode: 292
    - name: retained-startup-scratch
      emptyDir:
        sizeLimit: 16Mi
  nodeSelector:
    kubernetes.io/os: linux
    node-role.kubernetes.io/worker: "true"
  tolerations:
    - key: node.kubernetes.io/not-ready
      operator: Exists
      effect: NoExecute
    - key: node.kubernetes.io/unreachable
      operator: Exists
      effect: NoExecute
volumePermissions:
  enabled: false
  # Disabled for retained data: startup must not recursively change ownership.
  # repository restates the chart default so Renovate can see the pin.
  image:
    repository: bitnami/os-shell
    tag: "latest@sha256:481601c7f12a169eb8bfedbb6e434b8641abd5422eacf695e0c0823f15a00afc"

metrics:
  enabled: true
  # The exporter has a readiness probe, and a pod is Ready only when every
  # container is. A broken exporter therefore drops postgres-postgresql from
  # its Service endpoints and takes the database away from every app - the
  # same outage as an OOM, reached through the metrics sidecar. Pinned for
  # that reason, not for the metrics themselves.
  image:
    repository: bitnami/postgres-exporter
    tag: "latest@sha256:c6b5bd91427e5fad89c4995c198c9cf2851555cbc7d8f720d37f0ba201933a3b"
  serviceMonitor:
    enabled: true

files.templates/common.yaml:
defaultPodOptions:
  securityContext:
    fsGroup: 1000

controllers:
  main:
    containers:
      main:
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 10m
            memory: 64Mi
        env:
          TZ: "Asia/Jerusalem"
          PUID: "1000"
          PGID: "1000"
        probes:
          # Liveness restarts a container; it cannot fix a dependency outage,
          # it only adds a cold start on top of one. A Postgres restart took
          # the DB away for 93s and the stock 5x10s=50s threshold killed
          # mealie, paperless-ngx and vaultwarden mid-outage. 30x10s=300s
          # rides out a restart with room for a reschedule or WAL replay.
          #
          # Readiness matches it, which #1109 got wrong: "traffic drains"
          # assumes somewhere to drain to, and every app on this template is
          # single-replica, so failing readiness removes the only endpoint and
          # Traefik 502s. Ejecting is exactly as user-visible as restarting,
          # so it must not trigger sooner. Sonarr proved it: its /ping shares
          # the thread pool its download-client polling starves, so a busy
          # 20s stall tripped 5x10s=50s and blackholed a UI that was slow but
          # answering. Startup probe still gates rollouts, so a genuinely
          # broken new pod is caught before it ever serves traffic.
          liveness:
            spec:
              timeoutSeconds: 5
              failureThreshold: 30
          readiness:
            spec:
              timeoutSeconds: 5
              failureThreshold: 30
          startup:
            spec:
              failureThreshold: 30
              periodSeconds: 5

persistence:
  config:
    enabled: true
    type: persistentVolumeClaim
    # Must stay explicit. k3s recreates its local-path StorageClass (also
    # annotated default) on every restart, so it is always the newest default
    # and always wins the DefaultStorageClass newest-wins tiebreak. Omitting
    # this silently puts an RWX volume on node-local RWO storage.
    storageClass: nfs-pv
    size: 1Gi
    accessMode: ReadWriteMany
    globalMounts:
      - path: /config
  media:
    enabled: false
    existingClaim: media-library-pvc
    globalMounts:
      - path: /data
